reason: (1) Theory: for any complement W (any F2-linear projection pi with ker=V), weight of pi(x(P1+P2)) = sum of n-l parity functionals Tr(c_i x(P1+P2)); each mean is an additive character sum over the descended variety {(P1,P2): x(Pi) in V}, bounded by Weil/Lang-Weil (Bombieri) as O(deg * 2^{-dim/2}) relative, so per-coordinate bias -> 0 exponentially; no complement (random or Frobenius-adapted, a finite family) can sustain a constant relative deficit. Bias vanishing makes Hamming-NN keys uniform, so May-Ozerov reduces to exact sort-and-match: no exponent change. (2) Non-genericity: matching only uses the group law plus a membership/projection test on x; it is a group-op + fixed-predicate algorithm, so CGK / generic bounds apply up to the constant from the predicate; a projection with kernel V is just Semaev/descent's linear decomposition constraint relabelled. (3) Mechanism premise false: x(P1+P2) = x1+x2+lam^2+lam+a with lam=(y1+y2)/(x1+x2) is degree-high rational, not near-linear mod V; no Hamming-metric approximate additivity. Even a 5% constant deficit would give only engineering-class constant in a 2-list NN merge.
